survey: An analog clock seen from the front, standing upright on a green floor. Parts: a thick round orange bezel; a white dial inside it with 12 navy hour bars (longer at 12, 3, 6 and 9) and minute dots between them; a navy hour hand pointing to about 10 and a navy minute hand pointing to about 2, both on a round navy center cap; and a thin red second hand on the same pivot, with a short tail behind it. The face and bezel are round and even, and all three hands share one pivot. The clock has no feet, stand or base. It rests only on the curved bottom of its bezel, and its contact shadow sits on the floor.

errors.where: Bottom of the orange bezel, where it meets the floor
errors.what: The clock stands upright on its rounded rim with no feet, stand or flat base. A round desk clock balanced on its curved edge would roll or tip over. Real standing clocks have small feet or a flattened base. The shadow reads as resting on the floor, so this is a missing support part and not floating.

fix: Give the round orange clock two small rounded orange feet (or a short flat base) under the bezel at the bottom, so it stands steadily on the floor. Keep the face, hands and bezel unchanged.
